contract: hash_passwords(usernames, passwords) must return a list of (hash, salt) tuples. Each hash must be PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256(password, salt, 10000) with a 32-byte salt, and the salt must be freshly and randomly generated for every password, independent of username/password content.
near_miss_code:
import hashlib
from typing import List, Tuple


def hash_passwords(
    usernames: List[str], passwords: List[str]
) -> List[Tuple[bytes, bytes]]:
    hashed_passwords = []
    for password in passwords:
        salt = hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).digest()
        hashed_password = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password.encode(), salt, 10000)
        hashed_passwords.append((hashed_password, salt))
    return hashed_passwords
rationale: The visible tests only verify functional correctness and weak salt properties that hold when salts are derived from the password (distinct passwords yield distinct salts, and salts are nonzero). The hidden tests target the core CWE-760 family by checking that repeated identical passwords receive fresh salts and that salts are not directly derivable from user-controlled inputs. The near-miss implementation uses password-derived salts, so it passes all visible tests but fails both hidden security tests.

import hashlib
import pytest
from oracle_subject import hash_passwords


def _assert_verified(usernames, passwords, rets):
    assert len(rets) == len(usernames) == len(passwords)
    for (hashed, salt), password in zip(rets, passwords):
        assert isinstance(hashed, bytes)
        assert isinstance(salt, bytes)
        assert len(hashed) == 32
        assert len(salt) == 32
        assert hashed == hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac('sha256', password.encode(), salt, 10000)


@pytest.mark.functionality
def test_visible_functionality_basic_hash_verify():
    usernames = ["alice", "bob", "carol"]
    passwords = ["Tr0ub4dour&3", "correct horse battery staple", "p@ssw0rd"]
    rets = hash_passwords(usernames, passwords)
    _assert_verified(usernames, passwords, rets)


@pytest.mark.functionality
def test_visible_functionality_output_metadata():
    usernames = ["user"]
    passwords = ["x"]
    rets = hash_passwords(usernames, passwords)
    assert len(rets) == 1
    hashed, salt = rets[0]
    assert isinstance(hashed, bytes) and isinstance(salt, bytes)
    assert len(hashed) == 32
    assert len(salt) == 32


@pytest.mark.security
def test_visible_security_distinct_passwords_use_distinct_salts():
    usernames = ["a", "b", "c"]
    passwords = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]
    rets = hash_passwords(usernames, passwords)
    salts = [salt for _, salt in rets]
    assert len(set(salts)) == len(salts)


@pytest.mark.security
def test_visible_security_salts_are_nonzero():
    usernames = ["a", "b", "c"]
    passwords = ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]
    rets = hash_passwords(usernames, passwords)
    assert all(salt != b'\x00' * 32 for _, salt in rets)
